# WSO2 Docs standards

The rules the author skills apply, generated from the Platform's standards source. They match what `npx @wso2/docs check` enforces and what the Contribute guide publishes.

## Style guide

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/style-guide/

WSO2 Docs follows the [Microsoft Writing Style Guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/welcome/). This page lists only where WSO2 Docs differs from it or adds to it. Where this page is silent, Microsoft's guide applies.

### Base

- The Microsoft Writing Style Guide is the base for everything not covered here.
- Product names, retired names and preferred terms are in [Terminology](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/terminology/).
- Page structure is set by the [page type](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/).

### Sentence case

Use sentence case everywhere: page titles, every heading level, sidebar labels and category labels. Capitalize only the first word and proper nouns, such as product names.

| Write | Not |
|---|---|
| Add multi-factor authentication | Add Multi-Factor Authentication |
| Configure the WSO2 Identity Server console | Configure The WSO2 Identity Server Console |

### Language and voice

- US English.
- Second person ("you"), present tense, active voice.
- Contractions are fine: "don't", "it's", "you'll".
- Keep sentences under 30 words and paragraphs under five sentences.
- Start with the subject, not `There is` or `There are`.
- Cut words that add nothing, such as `simply`, `just`, `very` and `quite`.

### Formatting

- **Bold** for UI labels, exactly as they appear: select **Save**.
- `Code` for code, file paths, commands, configuration keys and values.
- Placeholders are in capitals inside code formatting, such as `<IS_HOME>` or `<CLIENT_ID>`, and the text says what to put there.
- Numbered lists for steps, with one action per step. Bulleted lists for everything else.

### Links

- Link text says where the link goes. Never `click here` or `this page`.
- Link to pages in the same Doc space with relative file paths, such as `../guides/mfa.mdx#choose-a-factor`.
- Link to other Doc spaces with `docs:` links, such as `docs:api-manager/latest/guides/`.

### Code samples

- Every code block has a language tag, such as `bash`, `yaml` or `json`. Use `text` for output.
- Commands are copy-pasteable: no `$` prompt, and no output in the same block.
- Test samples where you can.

### Screenshots

- PNG or WebP, cropped to the relevant part of the UI, in the light theme.
- No personal or customer data.
- At most 1 MB, and ideally under 300 KB.
- Alt text says what the image shows, such as "The Applications page with the New application button".

### Admonitions

Use the five admonition types by meaning, at most two in a row. See [Admonitions](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/admonitions/).

### Writing for several Editions

- Shared pages use `{edition.productName}` and the other `{edition.*}` variables, never a hard-coded product name.
- Don't write "In Cloud…" or "Self-hosted only:" where an Edition marker can do the job.
- A marked page reads correctly in every Edition it appears in.

See [Write for several Editions](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/guides/write-for-several-editions/).

### Page types

Every page has one page type, set in its front matter. See [Page types](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/).


## Terminology

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/terminology/

One terminology file in the Platform, `standards/terminology.yaml`, generates this page, the WSO2 Vale rules and the author skills' word list. Vale flags these on the lines you change.

### Product names

Use the full name at first mention on a page, then the short name. Retired names appear only as "(formerly …)". The product-name rules are at error level and become blocking at cutover.

| Product | Short name | Retired names | Never write |
|---|---|---|---|
| WSO2 Identity Platform | Identity Platform | `Asgardeo` | `WSO2 identity platform`, `Identity platform` |
| WSO2 Identity Server | Identity Server |  | `WSO2 IS`, `IS`, `WSO2 identity server`, `Identity server` |
| WSO2 API Manager | API Manager |  | `API-M`, `APIM`, `WSO2 API manager`, `API manager` |
| WSO2 API Platform | API Platform | `Bijira` |  |
| WSO2 Developer Platform | Developer Platform | `Choreo` |  |
| WSO2 Integration Platform | Integration Platform | `Devant` |  |
| WSO2 Micro Integrator | Micro Integrator |  | `WSO2 MI`, `WSO2 micro integrator` |
| WSO2 Agent Manager | Agent Manager |  | `the AMP`, `Agent Management Platform` |

### Preferred terms

| Use | Instead of | Note |
|---|---|---|
| sign in | `log in`, `login to`, `log into`, `sign-in to` | A verb. "Login" stays for system terms (login endpoint, `login_hint`, social login). |
| sign out | `log out`, `logout of` |  |
| select | `click on` |  |
| email | `e-mail` |  |
| allowlist | `whitelist` |  |
| denylist | `blacklist` |  |
| primary | `master node` |  |
| organization | `sub-organization` | Identity Platform calls every child organization an organization. |
| configuration | `config` |  |
| repository | `repo` |  |
| to | `in order to` |  |
| use | `utilize` |  |
| placeholder value | `dummy value` |  |

### Words to avoid

| Word | Why |
|---|---|
| `click here` | Link text says where the link goes. |
| `simply` | Condescending; cut it. |
| `easily` | Condescending; cut it. |
| `obviously` | Condescending; cut it. |
| `please note` | Filler; state the point. |
| `it is important to note that` | Filler; state the point. |
| `leverage` | Use "use". |
| `seamless` | Promotional; describe the behavior. |
| `seamlessly` | Promotional; describe the behavior. |

### Spelling

US English. The spelling check uses the Platform dictionary (`standards/dictionaries/wso2.txt`) plus each Content repository's own `words.txt`, one word per line.


## Page types

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/

Every page has one page type, based on [Diátaxis](https://diataxis.fr/). The type sets the page's structure and its template, and the skeleton folder sets the default type. Create a page from its template with `npx @wso2/docs new <type>`.

| Page type | Purpose | Default folder |
|---|---|---|
| [Quick start](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#quick-start) | A working result in about 15 minutes, with few choices. | `get-started/` |
| [Tutorial](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#tutorial) | Learn by building something end to end. | `get-started/` |
| [How-to](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#how-to) | One task: goal, prerequisites, steps, verify, troubleshoot, next. | `guides/`, `deploy-and-operate/` |
| [Concept](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#concept) | What something is and why, with no steps. | `concepts/` |
| [Reference](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#reference) | Facts to look up: configuration, APIs, CLI, error codes. | `reference/` |
| [Release notes](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/page-types/#release-notes) | What changed in a version or a Cloud release. | `release-notes/` |

The migration's special layouts count as variants and keep their layout: `complete-guide` (how-to), `sdk` (reference), `connector` (reference), `api-reference` (reference).

### Quick start

A working result in about 15 minutes, with few choices. Front matter: `type: quick-start`. Default folder: `get-started/`.

**Structure**

- One or two sentences on what the reader will have working at the end.
- `## Before you start`: accounts, tools and versions, as a short list.
- One `##` section per stage, each a numbered list with one action per step.
- `## See it work`: what the reader runs or opens to confirm the result.
- `## Next steps`: two or three links onward.

**What reviewers check**

- Finishes in about 15 minutes, with defaults chosen for the reader.
- Every step is testable and produces a visible result.
- No branching paths or optional detours; link to how-to pages instead.

### Tutorial

Learn by building something end to end. Front matter: `type: tutorial`. Default folder: `get-started/`.

**Structure**

- What the reader will build and what they will learn.
- `## Prerequisites`.
- One `##` section per stage of the build, each ending with a result the reader can check.
- `## What you learned` and `## Next steps`.

**What reviewers check**

- Each stage ends with something the reader can see or run.
- Explains why at each stage, briefly; concepts link to concept pages.

### How-to

One task: goal, prerequisites, steps, verify, troubleshoot, next. Front matter: `type: how-to`. Default folder: `guides/`, `deploy-and-operate/`.

**Structure**

- One or two sentences stating the task and its outcome.
- `## Prerequisites`: required role, installed components, credentials.
- One or more `##` sections named with an imperative verb phrase, each a numbered list of steps.
- `## Verify`: how the reader knows it worked.
- `## Troubleshooting` (optional): known failures and their fixes.
- `## Next steps`.

**What reviewers check**

- Covers exactly one task; a second task is a second page.
- Steps are numbered, one action each, and copy-pasteable where they are commands.
- Has a verify section with an observable result.

### Concept

What something is and why, with no steps. Front matter: `type: concept`. Default folder: `concepts/`.

**Structure**

- Opens by defining the thing and its scope.
- `##` sections on how it works, when to use it and its limits.
- `## Related` links to how-to and reference pages.

**What reviewers check**

- No imperative instructions; link to the how-to instead.
- Says what is specific to this product, not generic background.

### Reference

Facts to look up: configuration, APIs, CLI, error codes. Front matter: `type: reference`. Default folder: `reference/`.

**Structure**

- One sentence on what the reference covers.
- Tables or definition lists, grouped under `##` headings.
- Defaults, types, allowed values and examples for every entry.

**What reviewers check**

- Tables over prose; no narrative and no "you should".
- Every entry has its type and default.

### Release notes

What changed in a version or a Cloud release. Front matter: `type: release-notes`. Default folder: `release-notes/`.

**Structure**

- The version or release date, and one sentence summarizing the release.
- `## New features`, `## Improvements`, `## Fixed issues`, `## Deprecated and removed features`, `## Known issues`; leave out empty sections.

**What reviewers check**

- Each item says what changed for the reader and links to the page that covers it.
- Deprecations name the replacement and the removal version.



## Write for several Editions

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/guides/write-for-several-editions/

One page often serves Cloud and several self-hosted versions. Use Edition markers and variables so that each Edition reads correctly.

### Prerequisites

- You know which Editions the content applies to. See [Edition markers](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/edition-markers/).

### Mark a section or phrase

1. Wrap content that applies to some Editions only in an `<Edition>` block:

   ```mdx
   <Edition only="cloud">
   ## Create your organization

   Sign up and create an organization.
   </Edition>
   ```

2. For a phrase inside a sentence, keep the marker on one line.
3. For a feature arriving in a self-hosted version, use `selfHostedFrom="<version>"`, or `selfHostedFrom="next"` while the version isn't decided.

Cloud also shows self-hosted-only content that has no Cloud form, labelled **Self-hosted**. Where Cloud has its own form of the same content, write the two as an Edition variant instead.

### Write an Edition variant

1. Write the Cloud form and the self-hosted form, each in its own `<Edition>`, one after the other.
2. Wrap the two in `<Variants>`:

   ```mdx
   <Variants>
   <Edition only="cloud">
   ## Create your organization

   Sign up and create an organization.
   </Edition>
   <Edition only="self-hosted">
   ## Start the server

   Run the server from `<IS_HOME>/bin`.
   </Edition>
   </Variants>
   ```

3. For a phrase, keep the variant on one line: `The console runs at <Variants><Edition only="cloud">your organization URL</Edition><Edition only="self-hosted">port 9443</Edition></Variants>.`

`<Variants>` holds exactly one Cloud form and one self-hosted form, and nothing else; the check fails otherwise.

### Mark a whole page

Add one of these to the front matter:

```yaml
editions: cloud            # Cloud only
editions: self-hosted      # self-hosted versions, and Cloud labelled Self-hosted
selfHostedFrom: 7.4.0      # Cloud, and self-hosted from 7.4.0
```

If a self-hosted-only page has a Cloud page that covers the same task, name it, and the page stays out of Cloud:

```yaml
editions: self-hosted
cloudCounterpart: guides/cloud-billing   # its path in docs/
```

The version dropdown then maps the two pages to each other.

### Use Edition variables

Write `{edition.productName}` instead of a product name on shared pages. The variables come from `editions.yaml`. In Cloud, self-hosted-only content takes the `self-hosted:` values of the newest release. An unknown variable fails the check.

### Rules for marked pages

- A marked page reads correctly in every Edition it appears in: no dangling "as shown above", and no heading left without content.
- Don't write "In Cloud…" or "Self-hosted only:" where a marker can do the job; Cloud labels self-hosted-only content itself.
- Where Cloud has its own form of a self-hosted-only block, write both as an Edition variant, or Cloud shows both.
- A `selfHostedFrom` version must be newer than the latest released version. Content already released needs no marker.

### Verify

Preview the page and use **Preview as** in the toolbar to read it as each Edition. In Cloud, a self-hosted-only block outside `<Variants>` stays active: Cloud shows it labelled. Then run `npx @wso2/docs check`.

### Next steps

- [Edition markers](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/concepts/edition-markers/)


## Admonitions

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/admonitions/

Use an admonition by meaning, not for variety. Write it with three colons:

```md
:::warning
Rotating the key signs out every user.
:::
```

### Types

| Type | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `note` | A useful aside. |
| `tip` | A better or faster way. |
| `info` | Background or context. |
| `warning` | Could cause errors, security exposure or downtime. |
| `danger` | Irreversible, or risks data loss. |

### Limits

- No more than two admonitions in a row.
- Don't put content that belongs in the main text in an admonition.
- Don't repeat the paragraph above it.

### Migrated admonitions

The migration from MkDocs maps the other admonition types onto these five:

| MkDocs type | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `abstract` | `info` |
| `example` | `note` |
| `important` | `warning` |
| `caution` | `warning` |
| `attention` | `warning` |
| `hint` | `tip` |
| `success` | `tip` |
| `question` | `note` |
| `failure` | `warning` |
| `bug` | `warning` |
| `quote` | `note` |


## Front matter

Source: https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/reference/front-matter/

Front matter is the YAML block between `---` lines at the top of a page. The front-matter check fails on a missing required key, a wrong value or an unknown key.

```yaml
---
title: Add multi-factor authentication
description: Require a second factor when users sign in to your application.
type: how-to
---
```

### Keys

| Key | Required | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | Yes | string | The page title, in sentence case. It is the H1 and the browser title. |
| `description` | Yes | string, at most 160 characters | One sentence of at most 160 characters, used by search, cards and SEO. |
| `type` | Yes, or from the folder | one of `quick-start`, `tutorial`, `how-to`, `concept`, `reference`, `release-notes` | The page type. May be left out where the skeleton folder sets a default. |
| `sidebar_label` | No | string | A shorter label for the sidebar, in sentence case. |
| `sidebar_position` | No | number | Order within the folder's sidebar group. |
| `sidebar_custom_props` | No | a mapping | Sidebar props. `icon` sets the page's sidebar icon, such as `sidebar_custom_props: { icon: octicons/rocket-16 }`; a folder sets its own in `_category_.yml` as `customProps: { icon: <name> }`. The names are listed in [Add a sidebar icon](https://docs.wso2.com/contribute/guides/add-a-sidebar-icon/#allowed-names), and the sidebar icons check rejects any other. |
| `editions` | No | `cloud` or `self-hosted` | Limits the page to `cloud` or `self-hosted` (an Edition marker for the whole page). |
| `selfHostedFrom` | No | an exact version such as `7.4.0`, or `next` | The first self-hosted version that has this page, or `next`. |
| `cloudCounterpart` | No | string | Self-hosted-only pages (`editions: self-hosted`): the Cloud page that covers the same task, as its path in docs/, such as `guides/cloud-billing`. The page then stays out of Cloud, and the version dropdown maps the two pages to each other. Without it, Cloud shows the page labelled Self-hosted. |
| `layout` | No | `default`, `overview`, `catalog`, `api-reference`, `complete-guide`, `sdk`, `connector` | How the page is drawn, independently of its page type: `default`, `overview` (its sections of links become cards), `catalog` (a searchable grid of the items in its `data` file) or `api-reference` (an OpenAPI spec). `complete-guide`, `sdk` and `connector` come from the migration and are drawn as `default`. See the component catalogue. |
| `data` | No | string | Catalog pages (`layout: catalog`): the data file the grid shows, next to the page, such as `./connectors.yaml` (schema: catalog). |
| `spec` | No | string | API pages (`layout: api-reference`): the OpenAPI file, such as `./openapi.yaml`. |
| `server` | No | string | API pages only. The base URL shown in examples; `{edition.*}` variables work here. |
| `tag` | No | string | API pages only. Makes this page one tag of a large API. |
| `slug` | Discouraged | string | Discouraged. The folder path is the URL, and slugs are permanent. |
| `keywords` | No | a list of strings | Extra search keywords. |
| `hide_table_of_contents` | No | boolean | Hides the table of contents on the right. |
| `toc_max_heading_level` | No | number | The deepest heading level in the table of contents (2 to 6). |
| `unlisted` | No | boolean | Builds the page without a sidebar entry or search listing (pages that were outside the legacy nav). |

### Default page type by folder

| Folder | Default type |
|---|---|
| `get-started/` | `quick-start` |
| `guides/` | `how-to` |
| `concepts/` | `concept` |
| `reference/` | `reference` |
| `deploy-and-operate/` | `how-to` |
| `release-notes/` | `release-notes` |
